memory_block.body: Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

answer.rationale: The two observed declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), so the highest-leverage single slot is the funnel step that feeds both. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) and memory_31 (signup simplification produced a durable first-week activation lift in SMB) point at the same mechanism, and memory_31's 'durable' framing is the only inherited claim that survives past the first week. That also happens to defend the exact segment the competitor is attacking, without the retention damage flagged in memory_73. I am deliberately not chasing promotional_pricing: it would win SMB accounts back fastest, but memory_73 explicitly records materially worse 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it, which is the opposite of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. referral_incentive (memory_57) is clean but targets established customers, not the leaking top of funnel. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not the source of the decline. Verification choices: memory_86 because it is the memory my action rests on most directly and I want the original record's effect size, population, and whether the completion lift ever converted into revenue rather than just funnel motion; memory_91 because activation_messaging is my strongest alternative and its wording ('improved engagement', 'nudged') reads like proxy metrics with no retention or revenue readout \a it could be reranked above onboarding if the source record is stronger than the summary suggests. Key downstream risk: every supporting memory here measures completion, engagement, or first-week activation \a none measure qualified revenue at 90+ days. Optimizing a proxy can move accounts through the funnel faster while lowering their quality, exactly the failure mode memory_73 documents for pricing. So I will instrument this as a standard experiment with retention and revenue-quality as gating metrics, not completion rate alone, and treat memory_31's durability claim as unconfirmed until the archive corroborates it. If verification shows memory_86's lift was proxy-only or measured on a population unlike today's, I will fall back to activation_messaging at reduced scale rather than broadening onboarding changes.
